semantics: The result is the number of distinct values of the analysis variable on the records of the cell.
A missing value is not counted. For text, the empty text is a missing value.
A cell without records gives 0, not a missing result.
Text values are compared exactly, as they are stored. Case and blanks count.
count.subjects.takes: the values of the analysis variable on the records of one cell
count.subjects.title: Count of subjects

semantics: A pattern is text with exactly one mask. A mask is a run of the capital letter X, with or without one decimal point inside it and X on both sides of the point: "XX", "XX.X". The text before and after the mask is kept as it is: "(N=XX)" has "(N=" before and ")" after. A pattern with no mask or with two is refused.
The number is rounded by display.round.half_away_from_zero to as many decimals as the mask has X after its point, and to a whole number when the mask has no point.

A mask with a decimal point: the rounded number, without its sign, is padded with blanks on the left to the length of the mask. 9.52 under "( XX.X)" is "( 9.5)". A number that is longer than the mask is not cut.
A mask without a decimal point: the rounded number is not padded. 8 under "XXX" is "8".
A negative number has its minus sign before the padding: -3.3 under "XX.X" is "- 3.3". A number that rounds to zero has no sign.
A missing number gives a missing result.
For a mock shell the mask itself stands in place of the number, in lower case: "( xx.x)". No number is needed.
With the option rounding set to half_even, the number is rounded by display.round.half_even in place of the rule of statement 2. Statements 3 to 7 hold as they stand.
display.pattern.takes: one number and a pattern, such as "( XX.X)"
display.pattern.title: A number shown by a result pattern

semantics: The number is first written as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same double. That decimal is what is rounded, not the binary value behind it. 2.675 is rounded as 2.675, although the nearest double is a little below it.
The decimal is rounded to the asked count of decimals. A decimal exactly halfway between two results goes to the one farther from zero.
The result is text with exactly that count of decimals, and without a decimal point when the count is 0. It has no exponent and no thousands separator.
A result that is zero has no minus sign.
A missing number gives a missing result. Infinity and not-a-number are refused.
display.round.half_away_from_zero.takes: one number and the count of decimals to show, 0 to 15
display.round.half_away_from_zero.title: Round half away from zero

semantics: The number is first written as the shortest decimal that reads back as the same double, as in display.round.half_away_from_zero. That decimal is what is rounded, not the binary value behind it.

The decimal is rounded to the asked count of decimals. A decimal exactly halfway between two results goes to the one whose last digit is even: 0.125 gives 0.12, 0.135 gives 0.14, 2.5 gives 2 and 3.5 gives 4.
A decimal that is not exactly halfway goes to the nearer result, as in display.round.half_away_from_zero: the two rules differ at a half only.
The result is text with exactly that count of decimals, and without a decimal point when the count is 0. It has no exponent and no thousands separator.
A result that is zero has no minus sign.
A missing number gives a missing result. Infinity and not-a-number are refused.
display.round.half_even.takes: one number and the count of decimals to show, 0 to 15
display.round.half_even.title: Round half to even

semantics: The model records are those of model.ancova.lsmeans, statement 1. The result is one per analysis: the treatment grouping is compared, not split.

The dose of a group, by the option dose. grouping_value: the value of the grouping variable of the treatment grouping on the records of the group, which must be a number and the same on every model record of the group. group_rank: the place of the group in the order of the groups of the grouping, counted from 1.

model continuous_dose: y = mu + b * dose + the factor terms + the covariate terms + error, fitted by ordinary least squares to the model records, with the factors and the covariates of model.ancova.lsmeans, statement 2, and the variance of its statement 3. estimate: b. p_value: of the test of b = 0. With N - r residual degrees of freedom it is the F test of the dose term by Type III sums of squares (SAS PROC GLM; car::Anova, type 3), which for this term of one degree of freedom is the t test of b.

model linear_contrast: the model of model.ancova.lsmeans, statement 2, with the groups as a factor. estimate: the sum over the groups with model records of c[group] * tau[group], where c[group] is the dose of the group minus the mean of the doses of these groups, unweighted. p_value: of the test that this contrast is 0.

p_value is two-sided: the probability that |T| is at least |estimate / se|, where T has the t distribution with N - r degrees of freedom when the option df is residual, and the standard normal distribution when it is asymptotic.
Both results are missing when fewer than 2 groups have model records, when their doses are all equal, when N - r is less than 1, or when the estimate is not estimable.
model.ancova.dose_response.takes: the analysis records; the one grouping of the analysis, the treatment, which is compared; the factors and the covariates the analysis names
model.ancova.dose_response.title: Analysis of covariance, test of a dose-response trend over the treatment groups

semantics: The model records are the analysis records that belong to a group of the treatment grouping and have a value of the analysis variable, of every factor and of every covariate (missing as in rule I1).

The model is y = mu + tau[group] + the sum over the factors of beta[factor, level] + the sum over the covariates of gamma[covariate] * covariate + error, fitted by ordinary least squares to the model records, where y is the analysis variable. The levels of a factor are its distinct values on the model records, as text. A factor with one level on the model records is left out. No interaction is fitted.

The errors are taken as independent with one variance. It is estimated by the residual sum of squares divided by the residual degrees of freedom N - r, where N is the number of model records and r the rank of the design matrix.

lsmean of a group: the prediction of the model for that group with every covariate at its mean over the model records, averaged over the levels of every factor with the weights of the option weights. equal: each of the L levels of a factor weighs 1/L. proportional: a level weighs its number of model records divided by N (SAS PROC GLM, LSMEANS with OM; emmeans, weights proportional). Without interactions, the average over several factors is the sum of the averages over each.

se: the square root of l' V l, where l is the vector of coefficients that gives lsmean (statement 4) and V the estimated covariance matrix of the coefficients of the model, with the variance of statement 3.

lower_cl and upper_cl: lsmean minus and plus q * se, where q is the quantile at 1 - (1 - level / 100) / 2, level the option confidence_level, of the t distribution with N - r degrees of freedom when the option df is residual, and of the standard normal distribution when it is asymptotic.
A group without model records, or whose lsmean is not a linear combination of the rows of the design matrix (not estimable), gives missing results.
When N - r is less than 1, every result is missing.
model.ancova.lsmeans.takes: the analysis records; the one grouping of the analysis, the treatment, with results by group; the factors and the covariates the analysis names
model.ancova.lsmeans.title: Analysis of covariance, least-squares means by treatment group

semantics: The model records, the model and its variance are those of model.ancova.lsmeans, statements 1 to 3.

The option reference names one group of the treatment grouping. Every other group gives one result per operation, the comparison of that group with the reference. The reference itself gives no result.

estimate: the lsmean of the group minus the lsmean of the reference (model.ancova.lsmeans, statement 4), which is tau[group] - tau[reference]. In a model without interactions it does not depend on the weights of the LS means or on the values the covariates are taken at.
se: the square root of d' V d, where d is the vector of coefficients that gives the estimate and V the estimated covariance matrix of the coefficients (model.ancova.lsmeans, statement 5).

p_value: the probability that |T| is at least |estimate / se|, two-sided, where T has the t distribution with N - r degrees of freedom when the option df is residual, and the standard normal distribution when it is asymptotic. It is not adjusted for multiple comparisons.
lower_cl and upper_cl: estimate minus and plus q * se, with q of model.ancova.lsmeans, statement 6.
A group or a reference without model records, or a difference that is not estimable, gives missing results. When N - r is less than 1, every result is missing.
model.ancova.pairwise.takes: the analysis records; the one grouping of the analysis, the treatment, with results by group; the reference group, the factors and the covariates the analysis names
model.ancova.pairwise.title: Analysis of covariance, each treatment group against a reference group

semantics: The model records are the analysis records that belong to a group of the treatment grouping and have a value of the analysis variable, of the visit column (the option visit names exactly one), of the subject key, of every factor and of every covariate (missing as in rule I1). Two model records of one subject at one visit are an error.
The visits are the distinct values of the visit column on the model records, in increasing order: numbers by value, text by its characters. The last visit is the last of them.

The mean of a record is mu + tau[group] + alpha[visit] + (tau alpha)[group, visit] when the option treatment_by_visit is yes + the sum over the factors of beta[factor, level] + the sum over the covariates of gamma[covariate] * covariate. A column the option by_visit names, which must be a factor or a covariate, has an effect of its own at each visit: (beta alpha)[factor, level, visit] or delta[covariate, visit] * covariate is added. The levels of a factor are its distinct values on the model records, as text; a factor with one level is left out. A design matrix without full column rank gives missing results.

The records of one subject are normal with the covariance matrix Sigma of the visits, restricted to the subject's visits; subjects are independent. The option covariance: unstructured, every variance and covariance of the visits its own parameter; toeplitz, Sigma[j, k] = s[|j - k|], one parameter per distance between the positions j and k of two visits in the order of statement 2. In both, Sigma is linear in its parameters.

The parameters of Sigma are estimated by restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and the coefficients by generalized least squares with that Sigma; V = (X' Sigma^-1 X)^-1 over all records is the covariance matrix of the coefficients. A fit whose Sigma is not positive definite at the maximum, or that does not reach it, gives missing results.

lsmean of a group: the mean of statement 3 for that group with every covariate at its mean over the model records and every factor averaged over its levels with equal weights, at the last visit when the option at is last, or averaged over the visits with equal weights when it is average. It is l' b for a vector l of coefficients.

se: the square root of l' V l when the option df is satterthwaite, and of l' V_A l when it is kenward_roger_linear, where V_A = V + 2 V (the sum over i and j of W[i, j] (Q_ij - P_i V P_j)) V is the adjusted covariance of Kenward and Roger (1997) for parameters that Sigma is linear in: P_i = -X' S^-1 G_i S^-1 X and Q_ij = X' S^-1 G_i S^-1 G_j S^-1 X, with S the covariance of all records and G_i its derivative in parameter i.

The degrees of freedom of l: 2 (l' V l)^2 / (g' W g), where g is the gradient of l' V l in the parameters of Sigma and W is the inverse of the observed information of the restricted likelihood (minus its matrix of second derivatives) at the maximum. For one contrast this is the denominator degrees of freedom of Kenward and Roger and of Satterthwaite alike; the two options differ in se.

lower_cl and upper_cl: lsmean minus and plus q * se, where q is the quantile at 1 - (1 - level / 100) / 2, level the option confidence_level, of the t distribution with the degrees of freedom of statement 8.
A group without model records gives missing results.
model.mmrm.lsmeans.takes: the analysis records, one per subject and visit; the one grouping of the analysis, the treatment, with results by group; the visit, the factors and the covariates the analysis names
model.mmrm.lsmeans.title: Mixed model for repeated measures, least-squares means by treatment group

semantics: The model records, the model, its fit and the LS means are those of model.mmrm.lsmeans, statements 1 to 6, with the same options.

The option reference names one group of the treatment grouping. Every other group gives one result per operation, the comparison of that group with the reference. The reference itself gives no result.
estimate: the lsmean of the group minus the lsmean of the reference, l' b with l the difference of their vectors of coefficients.
se and the degrees of freedom: those of model.mmrm.lsmeans, statements 7 and 8, for this l.
p_value: the probability that |T| is at least |estimate / se|, two-sided, where T has the t distribution with those degrees of freedom. It is not adjusted for multiple comparisons.
lower_cl and upper_cl: estimate minus and plus q * se, with q of model.mmrm.lsmeans, statement 9.
A group or a reference without model records, or a fit that gives missing results (model.mmrm.lsmeans, statements 3 and 5), gives missing results.
model.mmrm.pairwise.takes: the analysis records, one per subject and visit; the one grouping of the analysis, the treatment, with results by group; the reference group, the visit, the factors and the covariates the analysis names
model.mmrm.pairwise.title: Mixed model for repeated measures, each treatment group against a reference group

semantics: The result is 100 times the numerator divided by the denominator.
The numerator is the result of the operation that the analysis references with the role NUMERATOR, in the same cell.

The denominator is the result of the operation that the analysis references with the role DENOMINATOR, in the analysis named there. It is the one result of that analysis whose groups are all groups of the cell. No such result, or more than one, is an error.
When the denominator is 0 or missing, the result is missing. It is never infinite.
When the numerator is missing, the result is missing.
The result is not rounded and not capped at 100.
percent.subjects.takes: two results that the analysis references, a numerator and a denominator
percent.subjects.title: Percent of subjects, with a referenced denominator

semantics: The values are the non-missing values of the analysis variable on the records of the cell.
n: the number of values. A cell without values gives 0.
mean: the sum of the values divided by n. Missing when n is 0.
sd: the square root of the sum of squared differences from the mean, divided by the denominator of the option sd_denominator. Missing when n is less than 2.
min and max: the smallest and the largest value. Missing when n is 0.
median, q1 and q3: the quantile at p = 1/2, 1/4 and 3/4 of the sorted values x[1] <= ... <= x[n], by the definition of the option quantile_definition. Missing when n is 0.

quantile_definition sas5 (SAS QNTLDEF=5, the default of SAS; R type 2): write n * p = j + g with j an integer and 0 <= g < 1. The quantile is x[j + 1] when g > 0, and (x[j] + x[j + 1]) / 2 when g = 0. For the three values of p here, g = 0 exactly when n * 4 * p is divisible by 4, so no tolerance is involved.

quantile_definition r7 (R type 7, the default of R and of NumPy): write (n - 1) * p = j + g with j an integer and 0 <= g < 1. The quantile is x[j + 1] + g * (x[j + 2] - x[j + 1]), and x[j + 1] when g = 0.
The median is the same number under both definitions.

sd: 0 when the smallest and the largest value are equal. This is decided by comparing the values, not by the arithmetic of statement 4, which can leave a rounding error of the mean (three values of 0.1).
summary.continuous.takes: the values of the analysis variable on the records of one cell
summary.continuous.title: Summary of a continuous variable

semantics: Missing values are left out. A group without values is left out.
With k groups and N values in all, the result is missing when k is less than 2 or N - k is less than 1.

SSB is the sum over the groups of n[i] * (mean[i] - grand mean)^2, and SSW the sum over all values of (value - mean of its group)^2. The statistic is F = (SSB / (k - 1)) / (SSW / (N - k)). The variances of the groups are taken as equal: this is not the Welch test.
p_value: the probability that an F variable with k - 1 and N - k degrees of freedom is at least F.

When no group holds two different values, SSW is 0 and F is not computed: the result is 0 if the groups do not all hold the same value, and missing if they do. This case is decided by comparing the values, not by a sum that rounding could leave just above 0.
test.anova.oneway.takes: the values of the analysis variable in each of k groups
test.anova.oneway.title: One-way analysis of variance

semantics: Rows and columns whose total is 0 are left out.
With fewer than 2 rows or fewer than 2 columns left, the result is missing.
The expected count of a cell is its row total times its column total, divided by the total N. The statistic is the sum over the cells of (count - expected)^2 / expected.
No continuity correction is applied, whatever the size of the table.
p_value: the probability that a chi-square variable with (r - 1) * (c - 1) degrees of freedom is at least the statistic.
Small expected counts change nothing and give no warning.
test.chisq.takes: a table of counts with r rows and c columns
test.chisq.title: Pearson chi-square test

semantics: The input is one table per stratum. Every table has the same r rows, the compared groups in their order, and the same c columns, the distinct values of the analysis variable in increasing order. A stratum is one combination of values of the strata columns (rule I12d).

A row or a column whose total over all strata is 0 is left out, and so is its score. A stratum with fewer than 2 subjects adds nothing. With fewer than 2 rows or fewer than 2 columns left, or no stratum left, the result is missing.

In a stratum with n subjects, let p be the vector of its row totals and q that of its column totals, each divided by n, and x its counts, row by row. Under the null hypothesis x has the mean m = n (p kron q) and the covariance V = n^2 / (n - 1) (diag(p) - p p') kron (diag(q) - q q').

With a matrix B per stratum (statement 5), G is the sum over the strata of B (x - m) and W the sum of B V B'. The statistic is G' W+ G, where W+ is the Moore-Penrose inverse of W, and its degrees of freedom are the rank of W. A singular value of W that is at most the largest one times the larger dimension of W times 2^-52 counts as 0 for both.

The option statistic chooses B. general_association: the Kronecker product of [I(r-1), 0] and [I(c-1), 0], so that the statistic compares every row with every column, with (r - 1)(c - 1) degrees of freedom when W has full rank. row_mean_scores: the Kronecker product of [I(r-1), 0] and the row vector a' of the column scores of the stratum, so that it compares the mean score of the rows, with r - 1 degrees of freedom when W has full rank.

The option scores gives the column scores of row_mean_scores. table: the values of the analysis variable, which must then be numbers. rank: in each stratum, the midrank of the column among the stratum's subjects, the sum of the column totals before it plus (its total + 1) / 2. With general_association the scores change nothing.
p_value: the probability that a chi-square variable with the degrees of freedom of statement 4 is at least the statistic. With 0 degrees of freedom the result is missing.
test.cmh.takes: per stratum, a table of counts with one row per compared group and one column per value of the analysis variable; the values themselves when the scores are the values
test.cmh.title: Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test of the groups against the values, controlling for strata

semantics: Rows and columns whose total is 0 are left out.
With fewer than 2 rows or fewer than 2 columns left, the result is missing.
The probability of a table with the row totals R[i], the column totals C[j] and the total N is the product of the R[i]! and the C[j]!, divided by N! and by the product of the factorials of its cells.

p_value: the sum of the probabilities of all tables with the row and column totals of the observed table whose probability is not larger than that of the observed table. The test is two-sided for every size of table.

"Not larger" allows a relative excess of 1e-7, so that tables of the same probability count whatever the rounding. This is the allowance of R's fisher.test for a 2 x 2 table; for a larger table see statement 8.

The sum is over every such table: no sampling and no approximation, for a 2 x 2 table and for a larger one. A table with more than 10,000,000 tables to sum is refused with an error, by both implementations.
A sum above 1 by rounding gives 1.

Implementations. Python sums over every table, for every size. R gives a 2 x 2 table to fisher.test and sums over every table itself for a larger one: there fisher.test allows a wider excess than statement 5 and counts a table that is more probable than the observed one by a relative 2.7e-7 or 3.2e-7, which changes the p-value by several percent.
test.fisher.exact.takes: a table of counts with r rows and c columns
test.fisher.exact.title: Fisher exact test
